titles: The P\'olya--Vinogradov inequality with $\log\log q$}
abstracts:
We prove that every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q\ge3$ has character sums
$\sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)$ of size at most $C\sqrt q\log\log q$, with an absolute constant $C$.
Montgomery and Vaughan proved this bound under the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and Paley
showed that it is optimal. The only input from outside the paper is the zero-free half-plane
$\Re s>7/8$ for Dirichlet $L$-functions. On the major arcs this half-plane gives a power saving for
twisted prime sums; on the minor arcs we prove a weak form of the Montgomery--Vaughan bound for
exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients, with Selberg's sieve as the only arithmetic
input. The same half-plane gives $|L'/L(1,\chi)|\ll\log\log q$ for every nonprincipal $\chi$
and, for every prime $q$, the two-sided bound
$-C\log q\log\log q\le\gamma_q\le C\log q$ for the Euler--Kronecker constant of the cyclotomic
field $\mathbb Q(\zeta_q)$.

titles: Supersymmetric Yang--Mills theories with several times reduce to ten dimensions}
Supersymmetric Yang--Mills theories with several times reduce to ten dimensions}
abstracts:
\input{abstract}

\medskip\noindent\textit{Keywords:} Supersymmetric Gauge Theory, Extended Supersymmetry, Space-Time Symmetries, Field Theories in Higher Dimensions

Supersymmetric Yang--Mills theories in signatures with several times are built by restricting the gaugino to the kernel of $k$ mutually orthogonal null vectors and letting the supersymmetry close on translations contracted with their product. We prove that every theory of this kind, defined by five axioms that Nishino's construction satisfies, has residual dimension $s+t-2k$ equal to ten (or to two, a degenerate case), and that its null vectors can be real only if $k\le\min(s,t)$. The cubic fermion terms reduce to a Fierz identity on the residual spinors, and that identity forces the dimension of the spinors to be $2(d-2)$ on a $d$-dimensional vector space, which happens only for $d=3,4,6,10$. With Majorana--Weyl spinors the signature must therefore satisfy $s-t\in\{8,0,-8\}$. There is no such theory in $(9+8n)+1$, $(10+8n)+2$, $(11+8n)+3$ or $(12+8n)+4$ for $n\ge1$, although it has been claimed that the existence proofs for the signatures $(9+m)+(1+m)$ carry over to these; the signatures $27+3$ and $19+3$ are among those excluded. For a single time the result does not depend on the construction: in $(9+8n)+1$ with $n\ge1$ every massless multiplet without tensor charges has at least $2^{2^{2+4n}}$ states, so a unitary theory with no tensor charges on its massless states has no massless vector multiplet.

titles: The bridge index and the nonorientable four-genus of knots with at most thirteen crossings}
abstracts:
We determine two invariants for knots that the KnotInfo database leaves open. KnotInfo lists
the bridge index of \btotal{} prime knots with thirteen crossings as either $3$ or $4$; we
prove that \bclosed{} of them have bridge index and meridional rank $4$, so the meridional
rank conjecture holds for them. The lower bound comes from representations of the knot
group in $\GL_4(\F_q)$ that send a meridian to a transvection or a reflection and fix no
nonzero vector. KnotInfo leaves the smooth nonorientable four-genus open for \ntotal{}
prime knots with eleven to thirteen crossings; we determine it for \nsettled{} of them and
narrow the interval for \nnarrowed{} more. Upper bounds come from pinch moves, lower bounds
from the Goeritz-lattice obstructions of Jabuka and Kelly evaluated by an exhaustive search
for lattice embeddings. Every bound is a certificate checked by a program independent of
the search that found it.

titles: Dense Algebraic Loci of Hodge Classes}
abstracts:
\itshape
We prove unconditionally that the Hodge conjecture is equivalent to two statements about abelian varieties, that the locus on which either statement holds is dense in every family and is either the whole family or a meagre set, that the real multiplications by $\sqrt6$ and by the cubic fields $\QQ(\zeta_{7})^{+}$ and $\QQ(\zeta_{9})^{+}$ are algebraic on explicit families of K3 surfaces, the cubic ones on the surfaces of Mumford type whose quaternion algebra is ramified at two real places, and that the Hodge conjecture holds on every power and every Hilbert scheme of points of the K3 surfaces of the one-dimensional Fricke families of levels $5$ and $7$, which carry complex multiplication by $\QQ(\sqrt{-5})$ and $\QQ(\sqrt{-7})$. For each of the two statements we build the object it needs next, a complex on a product of two Weil fourfolds and a class on an abelian fourteenfold, prove what it does, and prove at which step it stops; among the steps, every convolution of the Weil line bundles on $E_{0}^{8}$ whose shifts lie in seven consecutive integers fails the polarised criterion in eighteen of the twenty-eight arrangements of the shifts, an explicit curve of genus four makes the Prym map of cyclic triple covers \'etale onto the Weil domain of $\QQ(\sqrt{-3})$, and the conjecture for a class is equivalent to the vanishing of the mass gap of a multiple of it plus a complete intersection, which Koll\'ar's hypersurfaces show cannot be dropped for integral classes. Both statements remain open.

abstracts:
A composite number $n$ whose totient divides $n-1$ was known to have at
least fourteen prime factors. We prove that it has at least sixteen,
at least $16001$ if $(n-1)/\varphi(n)\ge3$, and more than $10^8$ if
$3\mid n$, and that $n<2^{2^{k-7}}$ if $n$ has $k$ prime factors. For
the companion equation $\varphi(n)\mid n+1$ we show that the nine known
solutions are the only ones with at most eight prime factors, and that
a further solution prime to $3$ has at least sixteen. Each
statement is reduced by hand to a finite computation, which independent
programs carry out. Lehmer's conjecture remains open, and we state the
assertion that would settle it.

titles: Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic}
abstracts:
We determine, for the heterotic string on the one-parameter family of
quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged
particles. The hundred and one families are labelled by the characters of a
symmetry group of order one hundred and twenty-five. Every Yukawa coupling
that this symmetry allows is a power of the modulus, and every other
coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly
one partner, so that fifty families are massless at the Fermat point and
none anywhere else, and at the Fermat point the masses are given in closed
form by the Gamma function. On the three other one-parameter families of
the same type, in weighted projective spaces, the symmetry no longer tells
the families apart and some families stay massless at every member. We
also prove that the Geometric Selection Conjecture is equivalent to the
existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and that a free
quotient of a Calabi--Yau complete intersection of any of the thirteen
one-parameter hypergeometric types never carries three families with the
standard embedding; on seven of these types, among them the sextic and
dectic pencils, no finite group acts freely at all.

titles: Reflexive Descent to Minimal Seeds in the Kreuzer--Skarke List}
abstracts:
Kreuzer and Skarke built the list of reflexive polytopes by growing it
from small seed polytopes. We ask how far a polytope can be from its seeds
when it is shrunk through reflexive polytopes only, one at a time and
without skipping any. Such a descent always exists and always ends at a
seed. In four dimensions no descent takes more than 348 steps, which
proves the conjecture of a uniform transition depth, and in two and three
dimensions the exact maxima are five and eleven. In four dimensions two
polytopes with thirty-seven lattice points need exactly twenty-two steps, so
the maximum lies between twenty-two and 348.

We fix the gauge of four-dimensional lattice Yang--Mills theory on a field
of straight lines that meets every plaquette in exactly one link, so that

titles: The Mirror Clause of the Geometric Selection Conjecture Is Empty}
abstracts:
The Geometric Selection Conjecture asks for a functional on the heterotic
landscape, built from the Weil--Petersson metric and invariant under mirror
symmetry, whose unique minimum is a phenomenologically viable vacuum. It was
shown in our paper on the Dwork quintic that the functional carries no
information beyond its minimum: the conjecture holds if and only if there is a
viable vacuum fixed by the mirror involution wherever that involution is
defined. We prove that the fixed-point clause is never satisfied. A vacuum fixed
by the mirror involution has a threefold isomorphic to its own mirror, hence
equal Hodge numbers $h^{1,1}=h^{2,1}$, vanishing Euler number and, on its
component of the landscape, a bundle with $c_3=0$; its net number of families is
therefore zero and it violates the three-family condition. Consequently no
vacuum built on the tangent bundle of any Calabi--Yau threefold, or on any
deformation of it, can be selected, and the conjecture is equivalent to the
bare statement that one viable vacuum exists on a component of the landscape
not of standard-embedding type, with no condition involving mirror
symmetry. The same holds when invariance under any compact group of
isometries containing the mirror involution is demanded. The existence
statement itself remains open.

titles: Ghosts in Poisson Brane Gases}
abstracts:
\itshape
A Poisson gas of branes with mass intensity $\nu$ dresses the graviton
propagator by the random entire function $\prod_k(1+p^2/t_k)$. We prove that
the gas average of the propagator equals
$p^{-2}\exp[-\int p^2\nu(\dd t)/(p^2+t)]$, so that the massive states carry
total weight $e^{-\nu(0,\infty)}-1<0$. For $\nu=\lambda(t)\,\dd t/t$ the
averaged spectrum consists of ghosts alone exactly when $\lambda\le1$, and
every average with a finite four-dimensional tadpole has states of both
signs. Frozen gases keep alternating residues.
\par\medskip\upshape\noindent
\textit{2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.} Primary 81T15, 60G55;
Secondary 30D15, 44A15, 30E25, 83C45.

titles: The Welch function is not third-order sum-free}

titles: An explicit exponent for the exceptional set of the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation}
abstracts:
\itshape
The Erd\H{o}s--Straus conjecture says that four divided by any integer greater than one is a sum of three unit fractions. In 1970 Vaughan showed that the integers up to $N$ for which this fails are few: their number is at most $N$ times the exponential of minus a positive constant times the two-thirds power of $\log N$, and his argument gives no value of the constant. We prove this bound with an explicit constant, given by an integral whose value is $0.6792$ and which a computation with directed rounding proves to exceed $0.67916$. The residue classes we sieve with include classes to moduli beyond the square root of each prime, which a recent theorem of Maynard lets us count.

titles: New Lower Bounds for Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres Numbers in Three and Four Dimensions}
abstracts: \itshape We construct eleven points in general position in four-dimensional space with no eight of them in convex position, and fifteen points in general position in three-dimensional space with no eight of them in convex position. titles: Regular Morley tetrahedra from $p$-secting planes}
abstracts: Tran replaced the trisecting planes of the Morley construction for a tetrahedron by $p$-secting planes, with one parameter for each pair of opposite edges, and conjectured that a regular Morley tetrahedron forces a pair of opposite edges whose four cross edges are equal. We show that every isosceles tetrahedron with three different edge lengths is a counterexample: its Morley tetrahedron is regular exactly when one vertex lies on one of four lines through the centre, and every such point occurs. When all three parameters equal $4$, only the regular tetrahedron remains.

titles: Regular Morley tetrahedra from $p$-secting planes}
abstracts: Morley's theorem says that the adjacent angle trisectors of a triangle meet in the vertices of an equilateral triangle. Tran carried the construction to a tetrahedron by trisecting its six dihedral angles and, more generally, by $p$-secting planes, with one parameter $e,f,g>1$ for each pair of opposite edges; the resulting tetrahedron is denoted $\mathcal M_{e,f,g}(ABCD)$. Tran showed that a regular Morley tetrahedron does not force the original tetrahedron to be regular, observed that in his examples some pair of opposite edges has four equal cross edges, and conjectured that this happens whenever $\mathcal M_{e,f,g}(ABCD)$ is regular. We show that the conjecture is false. We place an isosceles tetrahedron in the box $[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\times[-c,c]$ and prove that $\mathcal M_{e,f,g}(ABCD)$ is regular exactly when its vertex $A'$ differs from the centre of the box and lies on one of the four lines through the centre in the directions $(1,1,1)$, $(1,-1,-1)$, $(-1,1,-1)$ and $(-1,-1,1)$. Every interior point of these lines other than the centre occurs for exactly one triple of parameters. When $a$, $b$ and $c$ are pairwise different, no pair of opposite edges has four equal cross edges, so each of these tetrahedra is a counterexample. Two examples are given with the parameters in closed form. Finally, for quadrisecting planes, $e=f=g=4$, an isosceles tetrahedron has a regular Morley tetrahedron only if it is regular.

titles: Upper \texorpdfstring{$k$}{k}-star-forming sets and \texorpdfstring{$k$}{k}-independence in bipartite graphs}
abstracts: Sahbi conjectured that the $k$-independence number $\beta_k$ and the upper $k$-star-forming number $\SF_k$ agree on bipartite graphs, and in particular on chain graphs, and asked whether $\beta_3=\SF_3$ on triangle-free graphs. For every $k\ge3$ we give a connected bipartite graph on $3k+3$ vertices with $\beta_k=2k+2$ and $\SF_k\ge3k$. On chain graphs, however, $\beta_k=\SF_k$ for every $k$. We also show, answering another of his questions, that deciding whether a bipartite graph has a minimal $2$-star-forming set with at least $t$ vertices is NP-complete.

titles: Attaining the Entropy Limit\\ for Union-Closed Families}
abstracts:
We prove that every finite union-closed family with a nonempty member has an element that lies in at least $0.38288525996\ldots$ of its members. This number is the exact limit of the entropy method in the form developed by Liu and Jiang, and earlier work had come within a hundred-millionth of it without reaching it. The proof chooses the auxiliary function so that the two inequalities behind the method touch zero at a single point, and shows by a convexity argument that they stay nonnegative around it. With a global coupling of Jiang, the bound is strict for every family. We also prove the conjecture itself for every family of at most fifty-two members, two more than was known, by reducing a smallest counterexample to two families of down-sets of an unknown order and refuting them with a checked satisfiability proof.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} union-closed sets conjecture; entropy method; interval arithmetic; satisfiability

titles: Nilpotent-free spaces of $3\times 3$ matrices over the field with three elements}
abstracts: Wigderson conjectured that for every finite field $F$ and every $n\ge1$ there is a space of $n\times n$ matrices over $F$ of dimension $n^2-\binom n2$ whose only nilpotent element is zero. We show that every six-dimensional space of $3\times3$ matrices over $\F_3$ contains a nonzero nilpotent matrix, so the conjecture fails for $F=\F_3$ and $n=3$; the largest possible dimension is five.

titles: Two conjectures of Wormald on Hamilton cycles in tournaments}
abstracts: For a regular tournament on $d$ vertices with skew adjacency matrix $S$, the Hessian determinant $H$ that Wormald attached to its random blow-ups equals $d\det(d^2I+S^2)/\det(d^2I-S^2)$. Hence $H\neq0$ and $d/H$ is the square of a rational number, as Wormald conjectured. For the cyclic tournament it gives $\sqrt{d/H}=\bigl((d+1)^d+(d-1)^d\bigr)/\bigl((d+i)^d+(d-i)^d\bigr)$, so the associated constants tend to $\cosh 1/\cos 1=2.8559578925\ldots$; this proves a second conjecture of Wormald and identifies his numerical constant.
